hypothesis: V104 RL improvement over CE is partly attributable to its target distribution. Compare forward-KL distillation against existing reverse-KL RL with the same analytical target.
inputs: Existing V104 fold-local WARM, feature/reward transforms; V103 original/mean4 states; V101 training returns. No new image features or query access.
target: For identical normalized training states average ALREADY clipped advantages, then logtarget=logsoftmax((mean_adv+.25*logwarm)/.26). Same per-row weighting as V104; do not average per-row optimal probabilities. No heldout input to target construction.
training: Copy own fold WARM exactly. Fresh Adam lr .001, grad norm clip1,512 full-batch steps, float32 actor. Plain CE to float64 analytical target cast float32 for training. No added entropy, KL, checkpoint selection or early stopping. Existing WARM/CE/RL reused without updates.
qualification: One synthetic distillation optimizer step; verify target grouping and permutation/shift invariance, forward-KL CE identity, reverse-KL RL identity, finite decreasing synthetic loss; exact V104 normalizer/scale replay and all120 old models heldout probability/argmax replay before fitting.
readout: Seal all40 endpoints before new heldout scoring. Exact expectation primary, lowest-ID argmax secondary. Report dense/new-gain/old-change/regret and full probabilities. Compare RL-DISTILL, DISTILL-CE, DISTILL-WARM and all existing simple controls in every fold/seed.
decision: Positive RL increment over target-matched CE requires all4 stable stream comparisons >0; report every condition sign and means separately. Diagnostic result only; no deployment success.
limits: Shared-source training table; condition matching and repeated campaign adaptation preclude independent generalization claim. Frozen behavior continuation differs from deployed learned trajectories.
execution: CPU for tiny actor table; subsequent native experiments restricted to GPU4,5,6,7. No GPU wallclock limit; operation counts fixed per protocol. Create-only NAS, physical ledger, neutral commandline, reliable detached execution, full public aggregate delivery.
